div.div:
pervĭam , adv. per-via,
I.accessible (cf. pervius; “ante-class. and post-Aug.): angulos aedium perviam facitis, i. q. pervios,” Plaut. Aul. 3, 2, 24 ; Front. Orat. 1 fin. Mai: divus Augustus reprehendens Ti. Claudium ita loquitur: Scribis enim perviam ἀντὶ τοῦ obviam, Charis. p. 187 P.
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
